subject.title: [Feature]: Support running OpenClaw on devices without Linux / Node.js (inspired by MimiClaw)

question: Should OpenClaw define and support a runtime-neutral agent-core compatibility contract for embedded, WASM, or no-Node ports, or should MimiClaw-style ports remain independent external projects?
rationale: The current implementation is deliberately Node-hosted, and supporting this request would affect runtime ownership, plugin SDK boundaries, Gateway protocol, storage/session semantics, providers, tools, and security policy.

options.title: Keep As Runtime-Portability RFC
options.body: Use this issue to design the minimal schemas, conformance tests, and ownership boundaries before accepting embedded or WASM implementation work.

options.title: Scope To Plugin SDK Only
options.body: Route near-term language/runtime work through JSON-RPC plugin or harness APIs while leaving full no-Node OpenClaw ports outside the supported core contract.

options.title: Close As Not Planned
options.body: Decide OpenClaw remains Node-hosted and external projects such as MimiClaw are independent ports without compatibility promises.

recommendation.title: Keep As Runtime-Portability RFC
recommendation.body: Use this issue to design the minimal schemas, conformance tests, and ownership boundaries before accepting embedded or WASM implementation work.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already participated in the source-grounded keep-open discussion and has direct history on the runtime guard and harness direction surfaces.
